cards.explanation: The answer is for His people's sake. The LORD says, "For your sake, I will send to Babylon…" (Isaiah 43:14). He's talking to His own people, and He's the One who redeems them. The whole move is on their behalf, friends.

The answer is fugitives. The LORD says He will bring them all "…as fugitives, even the Chaldeans, in the ships in which they rejoice." (Isaiah 43:14). A fugitive is someone on the run. So the ships they were so happy about become part of that picture.

The answer is that they lie down, never to rise again. The LORD brings out the armies and warriors "…to lie down, never to rise again…" (Isaiah 43:17). Chariots, horses, the whole lineup, friends. Nothing in that verse has them getting back up.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Do not call to mind the former things; pay no attention to the things of old." (Isaiah 43:18). He's pointing them toward what comes next. And what comes next is a whole new thing.

The answer is in the wilderness. The LORD says, "…I will make a way in the wilderness and streams in the desert." (Isaiah 43:19). He says it right after "…I am about to do something new…" A wilderness doesn't usually come with a road, friends, so a way there is something new.

The answer is His chosen people. The LORD provides water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert "…to give drink to My chosen people." (Isaiah 43:20). The water has an address, and it's them. The jackals and ostriches honor Him because of it too (Isaiah 43:20).

The answer is True. The LORD says, "The people I formed for Myself will declare My praise." (Isaiah 43:21). Notice He says "will," not "might" and not "maybe." He formed them for Himself, friends, and praise is what He says they will declare.

The answer is that they have not called on Him. The LORD says, "But you have not called on Me, O Jacob, because you have grown weary of Me, O Israel." (Isaiah 43:22). I'll say it plainly, friends, this part is heavy. They have not called on Him, and He says they have grown weary of Him.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "I have not burdened you with offerings, nor wearied you with frankincense." (Isaiah 43:23). He hasn't loaded them down. And that sets up what He says next.

The answer is their sins. The LORD says, "But you have burdened Me with your sins; you have wearied Me with your iniquities." (Isaiah 43:24). It's a heavy line, friends. I think it's worth just letting it sit there.

The answer is that He blots them out. The LORD says, "I, yes I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake and remembers your sins no more." (Isaiah 43:25). That's the turn, friends. After that list, here comes the good news. Blotted out.

The answer is False. The LORD says He blots out their transgressions and "…remembers your sins no more." (Isaiah 43:25). He says He does it for His own sake. That's a promise worth reading twice, friends.

The answer is to argue the matter with Him. The LORD says, "Remind Me, let us argue the matter together. State your case, so that you may be vindicated." (Isaiah 43:26). He opens the floor, friends, and that's quite an invitation. He even says the goal is that they may be vindicated.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Your first father sinned, and your spokesmen rebelled against Me." (Isaiah 43:27). The text doesn't name the first father there, so I'll leave it right where the text does. The same verse adds that their spokesmen rebelled against Him.
The answer is destruction. The LORD says, "…I will devote Jacob to destruction and Israel to reproach." (Isaiah 43:28). It's a heavy one, friends, and I won't dress it up.
